NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Friday quashed the appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal assembly.A bench of justice Krishna Rao called the decision unsustainable under law and directed the speaker to reconsider and pass a reasoned order.The bench also asked the speaker to reach a fresh decision within 10 days.Following the West Bengal assembly elections earlier this year, assembly speaker Rathindra Bose had recognised Ritabrata Banerjee, leader of the rebel Trinamool Congress faction, as the leader of the opposition and Akhruzzaman as the chief whip.Challenging the speaker's decision, veteran Trinamool Congress MLA Sovandeb Chattopadhyay, a senior leader of the faction led by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, moved the Calcutta high court.Earlier, a division bench of the high court had allowed Ritabrata Banerjee and Akhruzzaman to continue in their respective positions on an interim basis for two months.After the interim period expired on October 18, Chattopadhyay approached the high court again, arguing that neither legislator had any legal right to continue in the posts as the interim arrangement had not been extended.He also alleged that both legislators continued to enjoy state-provided privileges attached to the offices of the leader of the opposition and chief whip despite having no legal authority to hold them.
Article Summary: The Calcutta high court quashed the appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal assembly. A bench of justice Krishna Rao called the decision unsustainable under law. The bench also asked the speaker to reach a fresh decision within 10 days.

Article Title: 'One community being favoured': Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President Murmu, cites low OBC, SC and ST representation in judiciary
Article Text:
Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai

Poll Vote & Share your view How significant is the issue of community representation in the higher judiciary? Very significant Somewhat significant Not significant at all Not sure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai on Friday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that judicial appointments increasingly favour candidates from a particular community, raising concerns over inadequate representation of OBCs, SCs, STs, minorities and women in the higher judiciary.Gavai expressed concern over a "growing disregard for diversity, inclusion and merit in judicial appointments and transfers", and sought presidential intervention to ensure equitable representation.In a letter dated November 27, Gavai alleged that a community comprising less than 5% of the country's population had accounted for more than 40% of Supreme Court judges in recent years, without naming the community."I am increasingly becoming concerned that recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he said."A community that is under 5% of the country's population has had over 40% representation in the Supreme Court which has risen manifold in the recent past. While I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable," he added.Clarifying that he was not opposed to candidates from forward communities being considered for judicial appointments, Gavai said his endeavour had always been to ensure a balance between different sections of society.Citing parliamentary data, Gavai said the representation of marginalised communities in the higher judiciary remained inadequate.According to figures presented by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025, only 22 Scheduled Caste, 16 Scheduled Tribe, 89 OBC and 37 minority candidates were among the 715 High Court judges appointed since 2018.He said roughly three out of every four appointees belonged to the general category, reflecting an imbalance in judicial appointments.Gavai further cited figures for appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, stating that nearly 80% of judicial appointments were from forward communities, while OBC representation remained below 14%."The Other Backward Classes, perhaps 40 to 50% of our people, have received under 14%. Within that pool, one community has been preferred at the Apex Court," he said.He also pointed out that the law ministry had informed a parliamentary committee about the "inequitable representation of backward and minority communities" in the higher judiciary. "Caste is not recorded for Supreme Court appointments, and that silence is itself part of the problem," he added.To underline the historical imbalance, Gavai referred to Professor George Gadbois's study of the Supreme Court's first four decades, which found that a community comprising around one-nineteenth of India's population accounted for more than a third of Supreme Court judgeships between 1950 and 1989.He said the composition of the apex court had remained largely unchanged despite 75 years of the Republic, attributing the persistence of such patterns to familiarity, networks and entrenched perceptions."Seventy-five years into the Republic, the profile of the Court has barely moved. Each of us bears some share of that failure, and I say so plainly. It is because I know how such patterns persist, through familiarity, through networks, and through unexamined ideas of who ‘looks like a Supreme Court judge’, that I can no longer stay silent," he said.Gavai also questioned recent transfers of High Court chief justices, alleging that merit had been overlooked and other considerations had influenced the decisions.He cited the case of a chief justice who was transferred from one High Court to a smaller court and subsequently to one of the country's smallest High Courts before being recommended for transfer to a prominent High Court.Gavai alleged that the latest recommendation came at the expense of another chief justice, whom he described as meritorious and hard-working, who was transferred to a smaller High Court to make way for the former.He said such decisions could demoralise the judges concerned and discourage other hardworking judicial officers, particularly those from marginalised communities.Explaining his involvement in the decisions, Gavai said he was part of the Collegium that recommended the first judge's transfers and headed it when the subsequent transfer was recommended. He also said he had led the Collegium that unanimously recommended the second judge's appointment as chief justice of a prestigious High Court on merit."It therefore raises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations has for no obvious reasons is now being recommended to be Chief Justice of a much bigger and prominent High Court," he said.Gavai said he had consistently sought to uphold diversity and inclusion during his tenure as a Collegium member and as Chief Justice of India, ensuring representation from forward communities as well as SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women in judicial appointments.However, he alleged that recent recommendations had departed from these principles, with candidates from one particular community being favoured over others."When I was a part of the collegium and was Chief Justice of India, I always followed the principles of diversity and inclusion. Adequate representation was ensured to different sections of the society including those belonging to forward section of the society and also to the marginalised section of the society including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women, while considering candidates for recommendation for elevation to High court and Supreme Court collegium of which I was a part and later headed it," he said."However, in the recent past disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard to principles of merit and inclusivity. Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalised communities including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of the society who are not from a particular community," he said."I may not be misunderstood as being opposed to any section of the society in so far as the candidate belonging to forward section are duly considered and my endeavour has always been to strike balance between all the sections. However, now there compelling circumstances which support the perception that increasingly recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he added.In his concluding appeal, Gavai urged President Murmu to acknowledge the issue and intervene as she deemed appropriate to ensure that all stakeholders were reminded of their constitutional duty to uphold equal representation.
Article Summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai writes to President Droupadi Murmu. He alleges that judicial appointments increasingly favour candidates from a particular community. He raises concerns over inadequate representation of OBCs, SCs, STs, minorities and women.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday issued contempt notices to top officers of the Tamil Nadu government over their failure to follow its order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon.Calling Tamil Nadu government's move a prima facie contempt of SC's order, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi expressed "pain and anguish" and warned that those who try to create constitutional chaos will not be spared."The first thing which comes to our mind is to express the word ALAS! as it would be relevant and appropriate to express in the present scenario. We say so for reasons assigned hereinafter and we say so with pain and anguish," the bench said.Also read: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in "The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos," it added.The apex court said that the executive authorities in the state were "acting on diktats of their political boss" and held that a prima facie contempt case was made out.The bench also suspended the board of trustees of the temple and appointed two retired HC judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over the management of the temple.The SC also handed over the security of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF.The Supreme Court also directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the Deepathoon on Saturday.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's order.On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. The order came while the Supreme Court was hearing challenges to the Madras High Court's directions on the ritual.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Friday issued contempt notices to top officers of the Tamil Nadu government over their failure to follow its order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon. The bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi expressed "pain and anguish" and warned that those who try to create constitutional chaos will not be spared. "The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos," it added.

Article Title: 'Don't waste court's time': SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana
Article Text:
SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, observing that those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the urgency of the plea, noting that the film had already been released in theatres and that those interested in watching it had already done so.The petitioner's counsel told the bench that the plea had been registered on November 23 but was yet to be listed for hearing."The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said.The counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film's depiction of the epic. Responding to this, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court."The CJI also remarked, "If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view. Don't waste time of the Court."As the counsel pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayana.Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.
Article Summary: SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana: Rise of a Legend. Those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective. The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayanas.

Article Title: 'If you offer zero seats, result will be zero': Congress MP Imran Masood's message to SP

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood on Friday renewed his criticism of INDIA bloc ally Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh . He questioned the Akhilesh-led party's reluctance to offer the grand old party more seats.Taking a swipe at SP, Saharanpur MP Masood said the Samajwadi Party's tally of 37 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh was made possible in part by Rahul Gandhi's contribution to the INDIA bloc's campaign."It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (Samajwadi Party)managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). We aren’t saying you didn’t contribute; we are saying that we, too, secured victories. We showed a big heart—but must it always be us who shows a big heart, every single time? Can’t you show a bit more generosity?" he told news agency ANI.The Congress MP also questioned the SP's approach to seat-sharing, saying the party should contest the seats itself if it was unwilling to give them to Congress."If you offer zero seats, the result will naturally be zero. Why don’t you contest these seats yourselves? You go ahead and win them—after all, you claim to have a formula for winnability." he added.Masood's latest remarks came a day after Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge publicly advised him to "talk less and work more", amid concerns that his repeated criticism of the SP could strain ties between the INDIA bloc allies.Addressing party workers at a Constitution Day programme in Lucknow on Thursday, Kharge acknowledged Masood's enthusiasm and his commitment to raising the party's concerns but underlined the importance of collective efforts.“Imran Masood ji bade josh ke saath apni baat rakhte hain. But more than statements, we have to work on the ground),” Kharge said.The Congress chief also acknowledged Masood's commitment and his consistent efforts to fight for the party in Parliament.

Article Title: Big, fat Bihar wedding makes global headlines
Article Text:
Global news outlet carried the headline, 'Politician hosts 4,00,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state', adding six helipads had been built for the purpose and 500 cooks had prepared a feast.

With 150 dishes on menu, finding a plate became the real challenge

The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh ’s daughter, Shivangi, over five days in his ancestral village of Nadwan in Patna district has created such a buzz that it has grabbed the attention of global media.The sheer scale of the ostentatious celebrations and feudal display of wealth and power, in the backdrop of the many criminal cases the MLA faces, became an irresistible story for the world media. That it’s happening in Bihar, the country’s poorest state, is an irony that echoes through the coverage.BBC observed that “the extravagant wedding in Bihar, a state where one in every three citizens is counted as multidimensionally poor, has been dubbed ‘a royal wedding’ and become a huge talking point.” It added that a political rival of the MLA has called for a probe into the source of money spent.The Guardian carried the headline, “Politician hosts 4,00,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state”, adding six helipads had been built for the purpose and 500 cooks had prepared a feast. Daily Mail called it a “big fat Indian wedding” in the “country’s poorest state”. It added the “scale was staggering even by standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings that last for days.”Held on Nov 25, Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s younger daughter Shivangi’s wedding to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit turned into an extraordinary spectacle with preparations for lakhs of guests, a horse race, a massive feast, luxury cars and five helipads.Anant had made it clear that invitations were not restricted to Bihar, extending them across India and even Pakistan. “Everyone who has shown us love will come. The public is like God to us; whoever comes from wherever will be a gift to me. Koi cinema thodi hai jo ticket lagega.”More than 10 bighas (6.2 acres) were developed into a grand venue featuring a Jaipur-inspired pavilion, a massive stage and imported flowers. The groom’s procession comprised 151 vehicles, while separate arrangements were made for guests and dignitaries.But food arrangements, despite 500 cooks and over 300 cooking stations, struggled to cope with the turnout.Videos showed disposable plates being thrown into the crowd with guests scrambling to catch them. Some used cardboard, newspapers, and even drinking glasses to carry food. Others were seen picking paneer directly from vessels, while a video purportedly showed a man falling into a “sabzi” vessel.Sticks were used to control the crowd. One guest described getting food there like winning a war, regretting that rasgullas had disappeared before he could get to them. With more than 150 dishes on the menu, finding a plate became the real challenge.The race featuring over 20 horses from Bihar, UP, Rajasthan and Delhi offered a Thar to the winner, a motorcycle to the runner-up, and a scooter to the second runner-up. Spectators climbed trees and high-tension electricity towers to watch, forcing the organisers to halt the competition and postpone the finale.The groom’s luxury car got stuck in traffic for hours, prompting the bride’s brothers to pull him out. Anant’s vintage open Jeep was used to bring him to the wedding stage.Traffic stretched for 8-10 km, leaving commuters and VIPs stranded. Bihar assembly speaker Prem Kumar’s convoy remained stuck for hours, while some walked through fields to reach the venue.Anant’s own arrival was equally dramatic. He stood up to look out of his SUV’s sunroof, waving an orange ‘gamcha’ amid cheering supporters. His entry looked less like a father arriving at his daughter’s wedding and more like a political roadshow.Meanwhile, allegations of animal cruelty during the celebrations have prompted an animal welfare activist to seek separate investigations into the alleged use of an iron “ankush” on a captive elephant and the horse-racing event.Chief scout Naresh Kadyan, master trainer of the Animal Welfare Board of India, has submitted a legal notice-cum-statutory representation to the Bihar government over alleged coercive handling of an elephant. He has also approached the Bihar assembly’s committee on petitions, seeking an independent inquiry into the horse-racing event held on Nov 25.With the bride’s ‘bidaai’ taking place Thursday, the MLA can breathe easy before he heads for jail on Dec 4 in a murder case. His bail has been cancelled by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh ’s daughter, Shivangi, over five days in his ancestral village of Nadwan in Patna district has grabbed the attention of global media. The sheer scale of the ostentatious celebrations and feudal display of wealth and power, in the backdrop of the many criminal cases the MLA faces, became an irresistible story for the world media.

Article Title: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
Article Text:
Smarting under the govt’s first defeat on the floor of Parliament, BJP has since made determined moves to shore up its numbers, helped considerably by fractures in the opposition camp.

Shah’s assurance may be added to delimitation bill, Cabinet nod today

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ending suspense, government Thursday moved to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30 during which it is expected to bring back the delimitation bills to implement the women’s quota law from 2029, which would increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength to 850 from 550, reflecting confidence in NDA that it will muster a two-thirds majority this time to secure the bill’s passage.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that government has requested Speaker Om Birla to reconvene Lok Sabha on November 30 and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan to call a sitting of the House on Dec 2 to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on Dec 3, 2026,” he said, suggesting government is hopeful of concluding its agenda in four days.This is the second attempt by government to secure passage of its ambitious legislative agenda. If passed, it will mark the biggest realignment of Lok Sabha constituencies since Independence. A united opposition had thwarted the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in a similarly convened session, of three days, from April 16.The move comes amid strong indications that government is confident of its numbers in the second trial of strength that the opposition is determined to force.In any case, it will be loath to risk another embarrassment; that too one during the build-up to assembly elections in UP and other states.Passage of the bill, which will ensure reservation of one-third seats in Lok Sabha and pave the way for a similar quota in assemblies, will give BJP a major campaign point in the upcoming polls to showcase its pro-women credentials.In an article on Thursday, PM Narendra Modi said the scuttling of the bill earlier this year “should fill our hearts with shame”, adding that a legislation aimed at giving adequate representation to women was prevented from being passed by one opposition party, in what was an attack at Congress.He assured women that “no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them.”Last time, among 528 MPs present in Lok Sabha, the bill had received support from 298 members while 230 opposed it, falling way short of the 352 needed for its passage.Smarting under the government’s first defeat on the floor of Parliament, BJP has since made determined moves to shore up its numbers, helped considerably by fractures in the opposition camp.The switchover of 20 of 29 Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MPs to NDA has boosted its numbers. Going by the buzz within government, it is also counting on support of 22 DMK MPs and eight of NCP-SP, who had voted against the bill last time along with TMC’s entire lot.Lok Sabha’s current strength is 540, with NDA’s tally at 321. The support of DMK and NCP-SP will take it to 351. The expected support from four YSR Congress MPs will take it closer to the 360-mark required in case all 540 MPs vote, which is unlikely as a few abstentions are expected to NDA’s advantage.Government has maintained secrecy about its potential new backers. DMK and NCP-SP have not announced support but have suggested that they can back the bill if states are not discriminated against — a threshold that government can easily meet by writing into the bill, which is already in Parliament, a clause providing for 50 per cent increase in seats across the board.Union minister Amit Shah had assured Lok Sabha in April that no state would suffer erosion in its relative strength in the lower House as the number of seats in each state would rise by around 50 per cent. The strength of state assemblies will be next to go up if the bill is passed. Shah’s assurance may be pencilled into the bill, which the Union cabinet headed by PM Narendra Modi is likely to clear Friday.A DMK MP told TOI that party chief MK Stalin will finalise their stand after looking at the bill, reiterating that southern states should not suffer. DMK has anyway drifted away from the opposition after Congress dumped it to align with CM Vijay-led TVK in Tamil Nadu.NCP MP Supriya Sule said “let the bill be out first”, suggesting her openness to the proposal. She said the bill may be good and needed to be studied first, and that opposition and government had in the past supported decisions which were in national interest.The hard part for the government is in the Lok Sabha, as its numbers are more favourably aligned in the Rajya Sabha.
Article Summary: Government moves to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30. It is expected to bring back the delimitation bills to implement the women’s quota law from 2029. A united opposition had thwarted the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in a similarly convened session, of three days, from April 16.

Article Title: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat
Article Text:
The fate of the contentious legislation that would take the strength of LS to around 850 seats would depend on these two regional parties, strategists said.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Despite repeatedly expressing apprehensions about a “sinister plan” behind the Modi government not proroguing the monsoon session for 106 days, the opposition was Thursday surprised by the BJP’s convening of the Parliament session , with the delimitation bill as the likely agenda. INDIA bloc is likely to meet Sunday to take stock of the situation.There is uncertainty in the opposition about the numbers game given the buzz around NCP-SP that has made equivocal statements in recent days. DMK’s stance is also being watched with wariness, though it was against the bill in the past. There is a feeling that government will not risk a loss of face on the bill again, and the convening of Parliament has raised concerns.The fate of the contentious legislation that would take the strength of LS to around 850 seats would depend on these two regional parties, strategists said.Congress’s KC Venugopal said, “For 106 days, they did not prorogue the monsoon session. There has been a complete lack of transparency... While the old delimitation bill was defeated, the new bill has not been circulated. Everybody is in the dark.”Amid speculation for more than three months over the delimitation bill, Congress spokespersons have been exuding confidence about the numbers, even vouching for DMK, which is not with the INDIA bloc anymore.Many have pointed out that DMK is a signatory to the recent unanimous resolution of the Tamil Nadu assembly, which had demanded that LS’s strength be frozen at 543 seats.Congress’s Jairam Ramesh said “the fight is on”, adding, “On Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, Modi government announces a special session, hoping it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass an amendment bill. Can there be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution?”CPM’s MA Baby termed the delimitation bill as designed to carry forward the divisive agenda of BJP-RSS. “I was in Parliament for 12 years but had never witnessed such surreptitious methods being used to subvert democracy,” he said.
Article Summary: The opposition was surprised by the BJP’s convening of the Parliament session. INDIA bloc is likely to meet Sunday to take stock of the situation. There is uncertainty in the opposition about the numbers game given the buzz around NCP- SP that has made equivocal statements in recent days.

Article Title: 'Does BJP's defeat rest only on my shoulders?' Masood hits out at SP after Kharge's warning
Article Text:
Imran Masood hits out at SP over seat sharing in UP

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood refused to temper his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, despite party chief Mallikarjun Kharge 's call for unity. Claiming he was being "cornered from all sides" and made a "villain", Masood questioned, "Does BJP 's defeat rest only on my shoulders?", taking another swipe at the INDIA bloc ally over its approach to the proposed alliance.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, Masood said Kharge had acknowledged his efforts and appreciated his work, while maintaining that he would continue to raise concerns in the Congress's interest."Kharge ji has acknowledged my efforts; he is appreciating my work. I am prepared to sacrifice my very life for the progress of my party. I am being cornered from all sides, as if I am a villain."Masood added, "I am making demands for my party; I am fighting for my party. I will always speak in the interest of my party. An alliance is being formed; does the entire responsibility of ousting the BJP rest solely on my shoulders? Does it not rest on yours (SP) as well?"The party MP also questioned the SP's approach to allocating constituencies, arguing that the Congress should not be offered seats where it had little chance of winning.“Give us seats; we can contest and win. We need both quality and quantity... You take the Chief Minister’s post. There is no dispute here regarding the Chief Minister. But why are you trying to undermine your ally? Why do you want to belittle your ally? You started launching direct attacks against me; why? I hadn’t said a single word against you," he said.He further argued that the Congress's contribution to the alliance should not be measured only by its past electoral performance."The Congress is zero. You keep reminding us of our standing, but if you think so little of our standing, why do you even need us? You have the formula for winnability; you have everything, so why do you need us at all?... We are zero—but wherever we align, we multiply the impact tenfold. It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (SP) managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). We aren’t saying you didn’t contribute; we are saying that we, too, secured victories. We showed a big heart, but must it always be us who shows a big heart, every single time? Can’t you show a bit more generosity?" he told ANI.The disagreement intensified after the SP reportedly offered 26 seats as a starting point and announced five candidates while negotiations were underway. Masood had objected to the move, saying: "We are not beggars... Somewhere, this is very hurtful: that you will dictate terms like this."On Thursday, Kharge, addressing the Congress's Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan in Lucknow, said Masood spoke with enthusiasm but stressed the need for collective effort. "But more than statements, we have to work on the ground," he said.The Congress is reportedly seeking around 130 seats, while the SP's initial offer was 26.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood refuses to temper his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. Claiming he was being "cornered from all sides" and made a "villain", Masood questioned, "Does BJP's defeat rest only on my shoulders?", taking another swipe at the INDIA bloc ally.

Article Title: Whatever is scarce wins
Article Text:
Two young Indians raised around Antwerp now teach big companies how to sound human on the internet. Their families learned the same lesson over a century: what you are really selling is trust.

In 2020, an 18-year-old in Antwerp was listening to a podcast in which one brother kept giving the other the same advice. The host was Ali Abdaal, a doctor turned YouTuber. His brother Taimur, a start-up founder, told him over several episodes that Twitter was where the founders were, and where the real conversation about technology and business was happening. Ali kept putting it off, though he came round in the end and now has some 350,000 followers there.The listener, Aadit Sheth, took the advice more seriously than the man it was meant for. On Twitter (I refuse to call it X), the feed was full of it. He found it freeing. Within six months he was boiling down two-hour interviews by Tim Ferriss and Joe Rogan into threads. There was no grand plan. Mostly, he told me, he wanted to make good use of his time.Six years on, Aadit has more than half a million followers on X and a company built on what he learned there.He and his co-founder, Arnav Kothari, run The Narrative Company, which helps large technology firms find their voice on X. They call it an AI-native social media agency. It is a curious label for a business whose best idea is that in a feed filling up with machine-made content, a human being is about to become the rarest thing on offer.Arnav grew up inside the diamond trade around Antwerp. His family's diamond and jewellery business, KGK, is about 120 years old and one of the largest in the world. He left a software strategy job in Boston and moved to Indore to hire an engineering team for it. The aim was to move buying that happened over calls and WhatsApp onto a platform. Six months in, the beta users did not love it, so the team reworked the design and relaunched three months later. Within three years the channel grew from nothing to $60m in annual sales, and getting there meant travelling between offices in India, Dubai, Antwerp, and New York to make it work for the teams using it. He has done sales for both businesses, and the contrast taught him what a brand is worth. In the family firm, a new account goes roughly like this: Someone already knows the head of procurement, there is an introduction, a dinner, and then, a contract. That ease is earned. Behind each introduction sit generations of trust and years of care in keeping it, and working inside the firm taught him to respect both. Flying between offices, he also noticed how much of that care now happens online, between visits.That gap is the whole subject of their work: how to make narratives clearer. I think it is also one of the most useful things to focus on.Every business wants a moat, something a rival cannot easily cross. When there is no moat, Arnav says, the moat is what people are already comfortable with. AI is making software, copy and advertising cheaper to produce. Efficiency is becoming the price of entry. What stays scarce is the feeling that a customer knows you and would choose you again.Aadit gets there through stories. He has been reading Satya Nadella's Hit Refresh, and was struck by the chapter on the birth of Nadella's son Zain, born with severe disabilities, and how fatherhood taught Nadella an empathy he had not had before. Aadit's own brother has special needs. And so, two paragraphs of a father's feelings moved him in a way nothing else could. People find their own lives inside someone else's story, and that is as true of a company as of a person. When Ivan Zhao tells how Notion nearly ran out of money, let go of almost everyone and moved to Kyoto to rebuild the product from scratch, people warm to the company and to what it stands for.Narrative began with that feeling. The founders admired how young firms such as Notion, Ramp and Anthropic talk to their users online, with humour and a sense that someone real is on the other side. Then they looked at the world's largest companies and found accounts that sounded like press releases. The idea was to carry the start-ups' community playbook into those older giants. Their answer is a hybrid: software in the back, people in front. Their tool, Nia, works like a "For You" feed for engagement: it uses AI to find conversations a company could usefully join, such as a developer describing an AI deployment problem a client could help with. The team then decides whether and how to take part, and Arnav, who leads Nia's development, works with clients on how it fits their needs. People stay in front because large companies still want a human to talk to, and because selling is still a human game: for now, it is people, not agents, who have to be persuaded to buy. The part no software can copy is taste: Aadit has spent six years learning, as a creator, what makes an audience trust an account."Whatever is scarce wins," Aadit told me. If everyone else is selling five hundred AI-generated ads, the winning move is to go the other way. His favourite example is Hector Serrano, who ran paid ads for the start-up Wispr Flow. By the account of the tech writer Lenny Rachitsky, Serrano made every ad himself for a year and a half. A few videos about how he did it travelled so far that Austin Rief, a co-founder of Morning Brew, publicly asked for a podcast on how Serrano had built a personal brand so fast. The résumé, in Aadit's view, used to record what you have done. Increasingly it shows how you think, in public. His advice to friends is blunt: open-source your thinking on X.Indians find this advice hard to take, and I don't think it is because we are shy. An American teenager applying to college writes an essay about who they are. Most Indian students never have to make that case until much later. We grow up inside a meritocracy whose promise is simple: do the work and you will win. It leaves out that someone has to know the work exists. Aadit points to Kunal Shah, the founder of CRED, who has spent the better part of a decade thinking out loud on X. A philosophy graduate from NMIMS, he built CRED and was then hired by Mark Zuckerberg to run WhatsApp worldwide. Aadit does not think that leap happens without a decade of public thinking behind it.Arnav's advice is also surprising. Don't rush it, he says. Build real knowledge first, because posting pays off far more when you have something to say. It is like going to the gym without a trainer: you will build a habit, but maybe with the wrong form. He does not post much himself. For three years at KGK he took roughly a hundred flights a year and had no settled base. The firm was making it easier to do business across distance while he went without a community of his own. He is clear now that he wants to spend his life helping people connect, and the new company is where he is starting: working out how companies can build real relationships with their audiences. That is what he wants to write about first. Maybe you haven't found what you want to say yet, he tells anxious friends, and that is fine.Which leaves the question hanging over his business: where does a good story end and a convenient fiction begin? And what makes a company's voice genuine when a team and software are helping it show up? Arnav has no formula, only a reasonable test. At 16, he co-founded a non-profit, Khilti Pari. When he pitched it to his school as an elective, the principal laughed and asked whether they were even incorporated. They were. It became the school's first student-created elective, drawing 10 to 15 students a year, and its exhibitions of paintings sourced from artists on Instagram raised crores of rupees over the years, enough to fund two vocational centres for girls in Rajasthan.On visits to the villages he spoke with the girls' families. Some fathers had been drinking and did not understand what the charity was trying to do. It made him doubt how much education alone could change while the girls stayed financially dependent, so the work moved towards jobs and independence, including training for government posts. One story is about bringing people together, the other about changing his mind after listening to the people he meant to help. Both still shape the problems he chooses, building communities among them. So before he tells a story about what he is building, he asks whether it still feels true. Can he sleep at night with it?The internet offers something fast and strange: You can now be known by people you will never meet, years before you need anything from them. And sometimes you do meet them. That is how the two founders met. Arnav messaged Aadit on LinkedIn to suggest coffee, and they spent most of it showing each other AI tools on their laptops. They became close friends, and then built the company together. Because who would have thought that when Arnav messaged Aadit on LinkedIn for a coffee and they spent most of the time showing each other little optimisations on their laptops, that eventually, they would build the Narrative Company together.
Article Summary: Two young Indians raised around Antwerp now teach big companies how to sound human on the internet. Their families learned the same lesson over a century: what you are really selling is trust. The Narrative Company helps large technology firms find their voice on X. They call it an AI-native social media agency.

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk Thursday said Leh district administration summoned him to execute a bond for maintaining peace ahead of Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections, scheduled for Dec 4.Though he appeared before the additional district magistrate Thursday, Wangchuk said he refused to sign the peace bond.“This morning after receiving the 19-page show cause notice from the office of additional magistrate in Leh, with a direction to appear before him at 3 pm, I complied and explained informally that there was no question of signing a peace bond or even an interim one since nothing I had said or done could breach peace in any way,” Wangchuk wrote on X.LAB is seeking a deferment of the elections due to harsh weather.“I have sought a week’s time for a formal response since the 19-page notice had many frivolous and unsubstantiated allegations which needed consultation with lawyers and transcription of speeches etc. The hearing was very courteous, and the young Magistrate agreed to one week’s time for reply,” he added.Wangchuk said, however, two hours after they came out, his lawyer received a letter demanding that he submit the reply by Saturday Nov 28. “This is a completely arbitrary and non-transparent process where a notice is served abruptly, and reply is demanded within two days after having clearly agreed to one week.”
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk says Leh district administration summoned him to execute a bond for maintaining peace ahead of Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections, scheduled for Dec 4. Wangchuk said he refused to sign the peace bond. He is seeking a deferment of the elections due to harsh weather.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: In October 2026, Joe Milton was on the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad; 41 days later, he led the Philadelphia Eagles to the biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history against his former team
Article Text:
Joe Milton, cut by the Dallas Cowboys after training camp and signed by the Philadelphia Eagles in mid-October, led the biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history on November 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

How a former Cowboys practice squad passer beat Dallas on Thanksgiving

The 21-point hole, the blocked punt and the final 50 seconds

Why the Eagles built their offense around Milton's arm

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What the win means for Joe Milton and a patchwork Eagles season

Joe Milton was a Cowboys practice squad quarterback in October. On Thanksgiving night in Arlington, he beat Dallas, his former team, from the other sideline. Playing for the Philadelphia Eagles, Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another score and led a rally from 21 points down. Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with two seconds left made it 39-38, the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history in NFL games. It was only Milton's third career start, and it came after Dallas cut him following training camp.Joe Milton did not need a perfect pocket for this one. Philadelphia trailed 21-3 late in the second quarter when he slid away from pressure, spotted DeVonta Smith one-on-one downfield and let it go for a 50-yard touchdown. Next Gen Stats tracked the ball at 64.4 yards in the air once the angle was counted. Milton said his first read was blocked by a linebacker and his second drifted too far away. So he escaped, looked up and trusted his arm. Smith had told him the week before to trust him on 50-50 balls.The second Smith score came late in the third quarter, a 45-yarder off play action after Milton rolled right, away from Kenny Clark. That made it 31-17.Smith ended with a career-high 200 yards on 11 catches and two touchdowns, even after getting banged up. Milton completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards, with three touchdown throws, one interception and a rushing touchdown. No Eagles quarterback had thrown two touchdowns of 45-plus yards in one game since Carson Wentz in 2019.He was named the game's MVP, then took his time leaving. Milton ate turkey on the field and walked into the locker room with a glass turkey-leg trophy almost 15 minutes after the final whistle. Coach Nick Sirianni, waiting to give his postgame speech, joked that someone should ask FOX analyst Tom Brady to let the Eagles have their quarterback back.For three quarters, this looked like a Dallas win. The Cowboys led 31-10 and still had a 14-point cushion early in the fourth. Philadelphia was thin, too. Jalen Hurts was out, and running back Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter with a stinger.Special teams cracked it open. Ty Robinson blocked a Bryan Anger punt, and Kenny Moore II scooped it up and ran it in to make it 31-24. Dak Prescott answered with a rushing touchdown for 38-24 with 10:19 left. Milton kept chipping away. Down eight inside 2:30, he took a shotgun snap, rolled right past two blitzers and hit Makai Lemon in the back of the end zone. That cut it to two.Then Robinson struck again, sacking Prescott on a fourth-down play. Philadelphia took over at its own 48 with 50 seconds left and no timeouts. Milton missed Darius Cooper, found Smith for nine, drew a pass interference flag on a throw toward Zach Ertz, then connected with Smith for five more. A false start on Markel Bell pushed them back, but it was close enough. Elliott's kick from 59 yards sailed through. Dallas fell to 5-7, and the pressure on coach Brian Schottenheimer grew.Milton's road here was messy. The New England Patriots took him in the sixth round in 2024, and Dallas traded for him in April 2025. He spent last season as a backup, then was cut after this summer's training camp and signed to the practice squad. Philadelphia saw an opening in mid-October. Hurts was dealing with blood clots, Andy Dalton had left, and Tanner McKee's rough outings made a change easy to justify. By Week 9 Milton was starting. He is the fourth Eagles quarterback to throw a pass this year.The Eagles adjusted, too. After the bye they moved away from under-center snaps and leaned on shotgun and pistol looks that suit his mobility and arm. Milton, 26, says he has worked for years with quarterback coach Donovan Dooley on throws made on the run, the exact skill behind the Lemon touchdown. His escapability was a big reason the coaches picked him over McKee in the first place. He prefers the nickname Mr. Rocket to Bazooka Joe, though nobody in Philadelphia was arguing about labels on Thursday.Teammates talked about his composure more than his arm. “The guy is a rock star, man,” Jordan Mailata said. Receiver Elijah Moore added that Milton takes over the huddle without wavering.Milton kept his own reading modest. He said he does not know what the game does for his career, only that the team played well and his confidence is up. He also said he was thankful, both to the Eagles and for the chance he had on Dallas' scout team.Some caution fits. Dallas has the league's worst defense, as the Inquirer noted, which matters when judging a 331-yard night. The Eagles' offense is also a patchwork right now. Hurts is out, Barkley was hurt, and tight end Dallas Goedert and cornerback Cooper DeJean both left early.Then there is Milton's future. Will Philadelphia want him back, and in what role? Will another team see this game and wonder if it can last? Those answers start in Arizona, where the Eagles head for Week 13. A fourth start there will tell more than any Thanksgiving highlight.
Article Summary: Joe Milton was a Cowboys practice squad quarterback in October. On Thanksgiving night in Arlington, he beat Dallas, his former team, from the other sideline. Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another score and led a rally from 21 points down. Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with two seconds left made it 39-38.

Article Title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current stepped up for struggling families with 400 gallons of milk and fresh produce
Article Text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Getty Images)

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current ownership extends beyond soccer

KC Current's food donation drive helps nearly 400 people

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have built a strong presence in Kansas City beyond the football field. While Patrick continues to make headlines with the Chiefs, the couple also has a stake in the city's women's soccer club, the Kansas City Current. Their involvement connects them to an organisation that has been working to make a difference beyond match days. One of its notable community efforts came in September 2024, when the club helped bring essential food supplies to hundreds of local residents.Brittany Mahomes was part of the ownership group that launched the Kansas City Current in 2020. Patrick joined the group in January 2023, becoming the first active NFL player to hold equity in a National Women's Soccer League team.The move gave the Mahomes family another connection to Kansas City's sporting community. Brittany, a former professional soccer player, has long supported the growth of women's football. Patrick's arrival added another high-profile name to the ownership group, which also includes Chris and Angie Long.But the club's work is not limited to building a successful team. Its community partnerships have created opportunities to support families facing everyday challenges, including food insecurity.That commitment took a practical form on September 23, 2024, when the KC Current joined Dairy Farmers of America, Harvesters and United Way of Greater Kansas City for a food distribution event at CPKC Stadium.Dairy Farmers of America donated 400 gallons of milk, while Harvesters supplied fresh produce. The drive helped nearly 400 adults and children in the area. Volunteers also prepared more than 200 bags of produce for distribution.The event brought the club's community mission directly to local families. Instead of a traditional donation announcement, the stadium became a collection and distribution point, with residents able to receive supplies through a drive-through arrangement.KC Current players Temwa Chawinga, Hailie Mace and Jereko also took part, helping load vehicles with milk and produce. United Way helped identify households that could benefit from the support, while its partnership with the club helped bring the participating organisations together.The initiative also reflected the value of the club's relationship with Dairy Farmers of America, which had partnered with the Current in 2024. The organisations later renewed their partnership in March 2025, with plans to continue dairy donation drives and events for families experiencing food insecurity.For the Mahomes family, the Current represents more than another sporting investment. The club's community efforts show how a professional sports organisation can use its reach, partnerships and platform to support the city it calls home.
Article Summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes own a stake in the Kansas City Current. The couple have been involved with the club since it was founded in 2020. KC Current's community efforts include a food donation drive in 2024. The drive helped nearly 400 adults and children in the area.

Article Title: Aaron Rodgers goes unclaimed by all 31 NFL teams after explosive Pittsburgh Steelers exit; 42-year-old quarterback becomes a free agent following public fallout with Mike McCarthy
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers goes unclaimed by all 31 NFL teams after explosive Pittsburgh Steelers exit; 42-year-old quarterback becomes a free agent following public fallout with Mike McCarthy (Image via Getty: Mike McCarthy and Aaron Rodgers)

Aaron Rodgers went from being benched to waived in 48 hours

Why have teams not claimed Aaron Rodgers?

San Francisco 49ers and Green Bay Packers linked to Aaron Rodgers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II criticized Aaron Rodgers in an interview with Gerry Dulac. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple of days before the game, that’s for sure.” What did Rodgers do?He went public with explosive attacks against head coach Mike McCarthy just days before the Steelers game against the Denver Broncos.The 42-year-old quarterback allegedly accused McCarthy of sleeping and snoring during multiple meetings, missing practices, walkthroughs, and film study, and mistakenly saying, “One, two, three, Packers!” instead of “One, two, three, Steelers!” at Steelers vs. Philadelphia Eagles halftime. Rodgers wanted to take over offensive playcalling, but McCarthy denied that.Rooney also told Dulac that Mike McCarthy is “as healthy as the rest of us” and added: “I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond.”On Nov. 23, a reporter asked Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy if he’d give other quarterbacks, like Mason Rudolph, a chance to play after two consecutive losses with Rodgers as the starter. McCarthy wholeheartedly chose Rodgers above all.The next day, on Nov. 24, McCarthy benched Rodgers and started Mason Rudolph for Friday night vs. the Denver Broncos. The next day, on Nov. 25, Rodgers missed the morning team meeting; owner Art Rooney II said that the franchise wasn’t going to beg Rodgers to stay.“If he believes his future lies elsewhere, he is free to leave. I promise you, we are not going to miss him,” Rooney told reporters.“We have other quality players in this squad, and we believe in the team we’re building. No individual is bigger than the franchise.Aaron is welcome to stay, but he must understand that decisions made by the coaching staff and management deserve respect. If he wants to remain a part of this project, he must be willing to follow the manager’s vision.”Pat McAfee interviewed Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show the same day he missed the team meeting [Nov. 25], where the Mike McCarthy allegations surfaced. The same day, on Nov. 25, the Steelers waived Rodgers. He cleared waivers and became a free agent on Nov. 26.Wednesday morning - missed team meeting.Wednesday afternoon - Pat McAfee interview.Wednesday night - waived by the team.It has been over a day since the veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers has gone unclaimed by all 31 teams. If we look at why each team has chosen not to sign him, several reasons might come up.For instance, some teams might think he’s like Brandon Aiyuk of the San Francisco 49ers, who disrespects the franchise and the coaching staff. Some teams might not want to risk a veteran quarterback at such a crucial midseason time. Some teams are happy just the way they are - they already have a starting quarterback.Dianna Russini, a former The Athletic reporter, asked several teams but there was no taker at the moment. Injuries can change situations in a second, but if this is Rodgers’ final season, his options seem limited.According to Steelers Depot’s Alex Kozora, the New England Patriots could theoretically have interest. Drake Maye is out. Tommy DeVito is the starter. But there’s no indication that the team’s interested.The Baltimore Ravens traded for Arizona Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett, and the Minnesota Vikings traded for Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins, so they may not want to add another veteran either.CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo predicts the San Francisco 49ers and the Green Bay Packers as the two possible destinations for the four-time NFL MVP. The 49ers could be nostalgic for Aaron Rodgers as he’s a California native and grew up a San Francisco 49ers fan.The 49ers passed on him in the 2005 NFL Draft, when the Green Bay Packers selected him as the first round 24th overall pick. If he enters the Bay, he may have to serve as a backup for Brock Purdy. Kyle Shanahan might want him considering his extensive experience.As for the Packers, that would be a homecoming for Rodgers. Of course, without Mike McCarthy - his fellow Super Bowl winning head coach.As per CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo, Rodgers is on good terms with both current Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur and quarterback Jordan Love. Plus, the timing couldn’t have been more perfect.This is seemingly his last season in the league, and what better way to close his NFL chapter than by retiring as a Green Bay Packer - just like he entered the league in the first place. If things don’t pan out and he remains unsigned midseason, he could very well retire.
Article Summary: Aaron Rodgers has gone unclaimed by all 31 NFL teams. Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II criticized Rodgers in an interview with Gerry Dulac. Rodgers went public with explosive attacks against head coach Mike McCarthy just days before the Steelers game against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers accused McCarthy of sleeping and snoring during multiple meetings, missing practices, walkthroughs, and film study.

Article Title: GTA 6 beats Valorant, Elden Ring and Diablo 4 combined to become biggest streaming launch ever
Article Text:
Image/Rockstar Games

GTA 6 breaks Valorant's record with 420 million hours watched in one week

TheBurntPeanut and IShowSpeed lead GTA 6's record-breaking streaming success

GTA 6 has broken a massive record becoming the biggest game launch ever on livestreaming. In the week after its release on Nov. 19, the game amassed a staggering 420 million hours of watch time. According to Streams Charts, this is almost three times higher than the previous record of Valorant in its closed beta in 2020. GTA 6 also attracted 7.91 million concurrent viewers, surpassing the launch week figures of several other popular titles.After years of waiting, GTA 6 finally arrived on November 19, and millions of players rushed to explore Rockstar Games' version of modern-day Florida. The excitement was not limited to people playing the game. Thousands of streamers also went live to share their gameplay with viewers.According to data shared by Streams Charts, GTA 6 collected 420 million hours watched during its first seven days. This made it the biggest game launch in livestreaming history.The record was much bigger than the previous one set by Valorant during its closed beta in April 2020. YouTube came next, followed closely by Kick. Both platforms had very similar numbers during the game's launch week.Popular streamers also played a big part in GTA 6's success. TheBurntPeanut became the most-watched GTA 6 streamer during the first week, collecting an impressive 11.43 million hours watched across his broadcasts. Most of his watch time came from YouTube.IShowSpeed also attracted huge attention. He recorded the highest number of viewers watching a single channel at the same time as he approached the end of his 52-hour GTA 6 gaming marathon. The streamer even broke down in tears after completing the game's story without sleeping.The Spanish streamer IlloJuan achieved the highest peak of viewers on several platforms.But the success was not just for the famous creators. Smaller streamers also got a big boost from the game’s launch. 1,056 channels set their highest ever viewers records while playing GTA 6. Of those, 193 channels attracted at least 10 times their usual record audience.The record-breaking launch has shown just how much excitement GTA 6 has created among players and streamers worldwide.
Article Summary: GTA 6 has broken a massive record becoming the biggest game launch ever on livestreaming. In the week after its release on Nov. 19, the game amassed a staggering 420 million hours of watch time. GTA 6 also attracted 7.91 million concurrent viewers, surpassing the launch week figures of several other popular titles. TheBurntPeanut and IShowSpeed lead GTA 6's record-breaking streaming success.

Article Title: "Nobody wins when the family feuds": Tom Brady calls out Aaron Rodgers for breaking an unwritten NFL locker room rule amid Mike McCarthy controversy
Article Text:

Tom Brady has made his position clear on Aaron Rodgers ' bitter Pittsburgh Steelers exit, questioning the quarterback's decision to take his disagreements with Mike McCarthy into the public domain. Speaking during Fox Sports' coverage of the Philadelphia Eagles-Dallas Cowboys Thanksgiving game, Brady stressed that an NFL locker room should remain a place of trust, even when players and coaches disagree. While he acknowledged Rodgers' Hall of Fame career, the former New England Patriots quarterback suggested that personal grievances should never outweigh responsibility towards teammates and the organisation.Aaron Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh quickly turned into a public dispute after the Steelers announced late Tuesday that they would bench him and start Mason Rudolph against the Denver Broncos. The decision came as a surprise, but Rodgers' response made the situation considerably more complicated.During an appearance on Pat McAfee's show, Rodgers launched a series of criticisms against McCarthy, questioning his preparation, leadership and understanding of the game.He alleged that the coach had fallen asleep during meetings, failed to watch enough film and even mistakenly led a "1-2-3, Packers!" chant at halftime.Reports also suggested Rodgers wanted play-calling responsibilities and gave Pittsburgh an ultimatum: grant his demand or release him. McCarthy subsequently confirmed that Rodgers "made an ultimatum." The Steelers chose to move on, officially releasing the veteran quarterback soon after his interview.Brady did not question Rodgers' ability or achievements. His criticism was directed at how the situation unfolded and what it said about the responsibilities players carry inside a team."The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it's a very sacred place. We shouldn't ever lose track of that as players. It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates, you're fighting with your coaches, you're always acting as a team together. Shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public, that's what I'll say."Brady also made a distinction between individual success and being a dependable teammate. He believes the latter should take priority, regardless of a player's standing in the league."Certainly a Hall of Fame career and he's a tremendous player and it has nothing to do with his play-style. I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what your team was trying to accomplish. That supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote."He finished his point with a line that captured his frustration with the entire episode: "Nobody wins when the family feuds."Tom Brady's comments carry additional weight because he also experienced difficult relationships with coaches during his career. His partnership with Bill Belichick in New England was not without friction. The quarterback acknowledged last year that a "natural tension" developed between them, which only ended when he left the Patriots.However, their disagreements rarely spilled into public arguments. Brady continued to acknowledge Belichick's contribution to their success, even after their professional relationship ended.He also reflected on that period while discussing the Rodgers situation, admitting neither man was perfect but emphasising the relationships they built along the way."I wasn't a perfect player and he wasn't a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we're so proud of now," Brady said. He added that his relationships with teammates and coaches meant more to him than winning Super Bowl trophies.Rob Gronkowski, Brady's former Patriots teammate, offered a similar assessment earlier on Thursday. He questioned whether Rodgers would get another NFL opportunity, suggesting that teams might be reluctant to bring in the controversy surrounding the veteran quarterback.Gronkowski also recalled how Brady dealt with disagreements behind closed doors."I've seen situations personally with my own eyes where [Brady] and coaches had disagreements. But there's one thing that Tom did different. He would dissect it all and then he would hold it in. And he would still do what's best for the team and for his teammates and for the organization."Tom Brady played under three head coaches during his NFL career: Belichick in New England, followed by Bruce Arians and Todd Bowles in Tampa Bay. His relationship with Belichick was particularly significant, making his comments more than a general lecture about team culture.Rodgers and McCarthy also have considerable history. Their partnership began in Green Bay in 2006 and eventually produced a Super Bowl title. McCarthy's appointment in Pittsburgh created the possibility of another chapter between the two, but their reunion ended in a public fallout instead.For Brady, the bigger disappointment appears to be how a professional disagreement became a public spectacle. His message was not that players should never challenge coaches. It was that those disagreements should not come at the expense of the people sharing the locker room.
Article Summary: Tom Brady questions Aaron Rodgers' decision to make Steelers dispute public. Brady stressed that an NFL locker room should remain a place of trust, even when players and coaches disagree. Former New England Patriots quarterback said personal grievances should never outweigh responsibility towards teammates and the organisation.

Article Title: 'Deny until you die': Ben Stokes makes explosive remark on Sandpapergate controversy

Former England captain Ben Stokes has urged those involved in the renewed Sandpapergate controversy to bring the matter to a close, warning that the continuing revelations are taking a toll on players, support staff and their families.Speaking at the launch of his podcast,, Stokes said the prolonged public debate was creating unnecessary stress and anxiety for people who had already been through a difficult episode.While calling for an end to the controversy, Stokes also held the Cricket Australia leadership of the time accountable for the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying those in charge "have a lot to answer for". He described the latest developments as a "deny until you die" saga and suggested that the full truth may not emerge anytime soon, given how deeply the issue has become embedded."For the sake of players, the staff, the management who were involved in this whole situation, for the sake of their families, for the sake of their friends, the best thing for it to do now would be for it just to stop," he said on hispodcast.Stokes also drew a parallel with his own experience of being under intense media scrutiny, explaining how such situations can affect people beyond those directly involved."It’s affecting people who do not deserve to be affected by this. Because I’ve been through something like this when you are so heavily in the media for something, I’ve seen what it’s done to people who don’t deserve to be put through stress, put through anxiety," he added.However, Stokes was equally critical of Cricket Australia's leadership during the original scandal, questioning the way the episode had been handled and the continued uncertainty surrounding it.“Whoever was in charge of Cricket Australia at the time has a lot to answer for this. It’s got so deep into it...that it’s almost just like ‘deny until you die’ one way or the other. I’ve been in the dressing room for long enough to form my own very well-educated guess on what I think has happened, but I don’t think in the close future we're going to hear what truly happened because it’s just so deep," he noted.The Sandpapergate debate has resurfaced nearly eight years after the infamous ball-tampering incident during the 2018 Cape Town Test. Fresh claims by former Australia opener Usman Khawaja in his memoir have brought the episode back into the spotlight, with the cricketer alleging that the entire team was aware of the ball-tampering plan.Khawaja's account has reportedly divided opinion within the Australian cricket fraternity and prompted fresh scrutiny of the original investigation, particularly regarding how extensively the incident was examined.The discussion has since widened, with several current and former cricketers weighing in on Khawaja's claims. His suggestion that Cape Town was not the only Test in which Australia tampered with the ball has further fuelled the controversy.With fresh accounts continuing to emerge, Stokes believes the renewed debate is now taking a human toll on those connected to the episode and has called for the matter to finally be put to rest.

The decision worked perfectly as England's bowlers dismantled the Australian batting line-up, bundling out the hosts for just 108 in 16.5 overs.Jamie Overton was the pick of the bowlers, claiming a sensational five-wicket haul for just 12 runs.
