CHRISTCHURCH: Rishabh Pant was out riding an electric bike in Christchurch on Wednesday evening when a chance encounter turned into an impromptu cricket match. Within minutes, India's star wicketkeeper-batter was padded up, hitting sixes and entertaining a bunch of amateur cricketers with a 54 off 21-ball blitz.Moments after spotting India's superstar in a tracksuit, 'The Open House Swingers' squad members identified him and started requesting pictures. The working professionals, unwinding during their routine Wednesday fixture, couldn't believe their luck, and little did they know what was in store next."I remember I was batting and there was chaos near the area where our squad was seated and had the gear. And I was like, 'What is this happening?' I had no idea then and just when I got out, I was informed that Rishabh Pant would be playing for us. I went, 'Okay, cool,' and couldn't believe our luck," club captain Harry Khan, who hails from Afghanistan and is a real estate agent in the city, tells"We are a social club, so we just manage to get the batting gear together for the game. And when Rishabh was set to go out to bat, the boys started finding the equipment. One glove from here and one from there and I don't even know if he wore a box (laughs). Even the pads weren't right but Pant wanted to have a good time. He was such a sport," adds Khan.The word quickly spread and play at Hagley Park came to a standstill when Pant, on what was supposed to be an off day for the team, started hitting sixes and was identified by other clubs.The opposition captain, however, wasn't aware until the second six off Pant's bat. He didn't bat under his own name, choosing "Stan Stan" for the day."The opposition captain had no idea (laughs) and he only found out after the second six. 'Oh, that's Rishabh, pretty cool,' he said when informed. There was no protest about fielding an international cricketer and everyone just enjoyed seeing him bat so closely. They initially thought we got a professional from somewhere. It was a great moment for our competition and provided great publicity. Even the organiser was present there that afternoon," says Khan, who leads the team of working professionals.Mohammad Safi, who works as a courier driver in Christchurch, was the one who spotted Pant riding an electric scooter and asked Rishabh for photos. After the pictures were done, he told Pant that they were short a player and asked if he would fancy batting. There was hesitation, but Rishabh agreed."After we were done with the pictures and he was getting back on the bike, I casually asked him if he wanted to bat for us. He used my cousin's profile name 'Stan', wore the keeping pads and we kind of rushed him when Harry got out," says Safi.When another wicket fell, it was Safi's turn to be Rishabh's batting partner and the two spent a lot of time in the middle before the anti-climax."It was a dream for me, man. Batting with India's wicketkeeper-batter, a legend of the game, and he was smoking sixes for fun. I just told him that I will give him strike. And during one of those attempts, I hit one close to the bowler. While I made my ground, Pant fell short and was run-out," recalls Safi, still disappointed.The news quickly spread to both the Indian and New Zealand camps. Morne Morkel "nearly fell" off his chair while watching the footage, and opposition captain Tom Latham was pleased to see Pant's experience going to LMS teams."Did he play?! How'd he go?" Latham said at his New Zealand press conference. "That's brilliant!"It's great. He's obviously a real character of the game, is Rishabh."It's great for him to be giving his experience back to LMS (Last Man Standing) teams!"For The Open House Swingers, it was publicity like never before. What began as a routine Wednesday fixture at Hagley Park turned into an unforgettable evening, with a chance encounter on an electric bike bringing a Test superstar into their midst and leaving the Christchurch social cricket community with a story to cherish.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant was out riding an electric bike in Christchurch on Wednesday evening when a chance encounter turned into an impromptu cricket match. Article Title: Who won Bills vs Chiefs Thanksgiving game? Inside the dramatic final moments of Josh Allen vs Patrick Mahomes
Article Text:
​Josh Allen gets the better of Patrick Mahomes in 13-10 thriller (Getty Images)​

Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Bass's last-second kick

Josh Allen's turnovers and the questions left for both teams

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tyler Bass booted a 57-yard field goal as time ran out Thursday night, and the Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a wet, ugly Thanksgiving game. Buffalo moves to 10-1. Kansas City falls to 8-3 and now faces a hard climb to the AFC's top seed. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes did not decide this one. Special teams did, with a tipped punt, a missed Chiefs kick and one long swing of Bass's leg. Bass had also tied it at 10-10 in the fourth quarter.Buffalo led 7-3 at halftime, and the score said plenty about the conditions. Neither offense could get going. Kansas City took a 10-7 lead on its first drive of the third quarter, which ended a remarkable run for the Bills' defense. Buffalo had not allowed a touchdown since the opening quarter of its Week 8 win over Baltimore. That stretch covered 46 drives and tied the 2008 Ravens for the longest in the past 20 NFL seasons.Then the kickers took over.Bass tied the game with a 54-yarder. Harrison Butker answered with a miss from 46 yards. Buffalo punted, and rookie Tommy Doman Jr. sent it 57 yards, with Josh Downs forced out of bounds at the Kansas City 7.The Chiefs went three-and-out, but Matt Araiza's 38-yard punt was a poor one and gave the Bills the ball near midfield. They could not score, so Doman punted again, this time 46 yards. Kansas City started at its own 11 with 26 seconds left.The last punt decided it. Joe Andreessen got a hand on Araiza's kick, and Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Kansas City 39. That left Bass a 57-yard try in bad weather. He made it.That is the odd part of this win. The Bills did not beat Kansas City with their best players. They beat the Chiefs with a rookie punter, a tipped ball and a kicker who needed 57 yards.Allen threw two interceptions in the red zone. One bounced off Khalil Shakir's hands, so it is hard to pin entirely on the quarterback, though the throw was not clean either. Still, the numbers are getting harder to ignore. Allen has thrown an interception in five straight games, seven in all. The wet field explains some of Thursday.It does not explain the weeks before. With a tough run of games ahead, the habit matters more now.Buffalo's defense deserves credit, and it will still get an asterisk. During the touchdown-free streak it faced backup quarterbacks, and Mahomes was working in wet conditions. Fair or not, that is the criticism. The Bills can only play who is on the schedule.For Kansas City, the loss hurts in the standings. The Chiefs still have a path to the playoffs, but the No. 1 seed looks far away. This was the 11th meeting between Allen and Mahomes, and it may be the one that had the least to do with either of them.
Article Summary: Tyler Bass kicked a 57-yard field goal as time ran out, and the Bills beat the Chiefs 13-10. Buffalo moves to 10-1. Kansas City falls to 8-3 and now faces a hard climb to the AFC's top seed.

The incident reportedly left then head coach Justin Langer furious.Whateley said Langer gave the players a strong dressing-room lecture after the day's play.He reportedly "grabbed a baggy green and wiped it on his backside to illustrate what he thought the players were doing to Australian cricket".CODE Sports also named Travis Head as the player who strongly opposed the suggestion. Head, who was making his Test debut at the time, reportedly responded by saying, "You’re f***ing kidding me.We’re not doing that sh** again".The report does not make it clear whether Lyon's alleged request was serious or intended as a joke. However, coming soon after the ball-tampering scandal, the suggestion reportedly drew an immediate response from Paine and Langer.Head was already seen as a mature player and a leader at a young age. Before making his Test debut, he had been a regular part of Australia's ODI and T20I teams since 2018. He had also become South Australia's youngest-ever first-class captain at the age of 21.Head has since gone on to become Australia's vice-captain.Usman Khawaja also spoke about the incident on The Grade Cricketer podcast. While he did not identify Lyon as the player involved, he supported Whateley's account and described Langer's reaction as "one of the all time greats".“I remember it was very targeted at one player, then the whole team," he recalled.“What I remember from it was like, ‘If any of you guys ever even think about this again, you will not play for Australia again.’“He didn’t actually get a hat ...but his metaphor was, ‘This is what you’re doing with the baggy green right now.’”The latest report comes on the same day Cricket Australia confirmed details of an independent forum into the Sandpapergate scandal. Respected barrister Fiona McLeod SC will head the forum.It also comes after reports that Lyon has been dropped from Australia's squad for the first Test against New Zealand, which begins in Perth on December 9.However, there is no suggestion that the 39-year-old's reported omission from the squad has anything to do with the latest claims.
Article Summary: Nathan Lyon named as player who allegedly suggested using mints on the ball during the team's first Test after the Sandpapergate scandal. Travis Head reportedly objected to the idea, saying, "You're f***ing kidding me" Usman Khawaja also spoke about the incident, describing Justin Langer's reaction as "one of the all time greats"

Article Title: A Chandigarh woman on her way to receive 'Best Advocate Award' was left waiting for nearly two hours after her booked cab failed to arrive; consumer commission orders travel agency to pay Rs 10,000
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

5 key highlights





CHANDIGARH: A cab that never arrived cost a Chandigarh woman nearly two hours on the morning she was supposed to travel to Ludhiana for an award ceremony. With no response from the travel agency, she had to find another vehicle to make the journey. The incident dates back to August 28, 2022. Nearly four years later, a Punjab consumer commission has held the travel agency responsible for failing to provide the promised service and ordered it to pay Rs 10,000 in compensation and litigation expenses.The dispute centred on a booking made three days before the scheduled journey. The woman had contacted the agency on August 25 to arrange a Chandigarh-Ludhiana round trip. She was due to attend a function in Ludhiana, where she was reportedly set to receive the Best Advocate Award. The fare became part of the dispute. While the agency initially quoted Rs 2,200, the woman negotiated it down to Rs 2,000, an arrangement reflected in their WhatsApp conversation. She claimed that she had also paid Rs 1,000 in advance and was assured that the cab would pick her up from her residence at 6.30 am.That assurance was not honoured. When the vehicle failed to arrive, the woman tried reaching the agency but allegedly received no information about the delay.After waiting for around two hours, she made alternative transport arrangements and continued to Ludhiana. She subsequently approached the consumer commission, alleging harassment and embarrassment caused by the agency's failure. The agency disputed her version, arguing that the booking was never confirmed because she had not deposited 50% of the agreed fare as advance. It maintained that its representative had shared the number of an independent cab driver on August 27 and instructed her to contact him directly. It also denied receiving the Rs 1,000 payment or assuring her of a confirmed pickup.The commission's examination of the WhatsApp messages established that the two parties had discussed and agreed on the booking and fare. While the woman could not produce evidence of the alleged advance payment, the commission found that the agency could not deny that a cab had been booked but was not provided on time. The woman had also sought relief on the ground that she missed an important award ceremony. However, the commission noted that she had submitted no documentary evidence to establish that she was actually scheduled to receive the award or had missed the function.It nevertheless held that the absence of proof regarding the award did not excuse the agency's failure to provide the vehicle at the promised time. The commission partly allowed her complaint and directed the travel agency to pay Rs 10,000 towards deficiency in service, mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses within 30 days.1. The travel agency initially quoted Rs 2,200 but agreed to Rs 2,000 after negotiations on WhatsApp. The woman claimed she also paid Rs 1,000 in advance and was assured of a 6.30 am pickup.3. When the cab failed to arrive and the agency allegedly did not respond, the woman waited for nearly two hours before arranging alternative transport to reach Ludhiana.4. The agency denied confirming the booking, claiming she had not paid the required 50% advance. The consumer commission, however, found that WhatsApp messages established that the booking and fare had been discussed and agreed upon.5. It noted that the woman had not provided documentary proof that she was due to receive the award or had missed the ceremony.

Article Title: 'I love someone else': Day before engagement, father kills daughter who rejected groom chosen by family; hangs body to fake suicide
Article Text:
A woman named A Kalyani was reportedly killed by her father in Adilabad for refusing an arranged marriage





HYDERABAD: A day before her betrothal, an 18-year-old woman in Adilabad allegedly told her family that she did not want marry the man they had chosen for her as she was in love with another man.Hours later, her father allegedly smothered her to death while she slept, hanged her body from a roof beam to pass it off as suicide and hurriedly cremated the body before relatives could arrive, police said.Police arrested accused Kailash on Thursday after questioning. The woman, A Kalyani, was killed at the family’s home in Umri village in Adilabad in the early hours of Nov 24, police said.Cops first became suspicious over the haste with which the family conducted the last rites. Narnoor police had received an alert from Umri residents around 8.30 am on Nov 24 about Kalyani’s suspicious death.“By the time our team reached the village, the cremation was almost completed. The woman’s father claimed that she hanged herself at home and they noticed the body at 5.30 am. We became suspicious since the family tried to finish the final rites without waiting for relatives within three hours after her death.Also, in their community, unmarried deceased are buried and not cremated as per custom,” Adilabad district SP Akhil Mahajan said.Umri panchayat secretary B Rajanna had lodged a complaint with Narnoor police a day after her death, stating that Kalyani’s marriage had been fixed and her engagement was scheduled for Nov 25. He alleged that she was in love with another man and Kailash killed her fearing the affair would bring disgrace to his family.Police registered a murder case under Section 103(1) of the BNS.Utnoor additional SP Ruthwik Sai Kotte said Kalyani had told her family on the night of Nov 23 that she was not interested in the proposed marriage because she was in love with another man.“Kailash felt that his daughter’s decision might bring disrepute to the family and smothered her to death during the early hours of Nov 24 when she was asleep,” the ASP said.Police said Kailash then tied a stole around his daughter’s neck and hanged her body from a roof beam inside the house in an attempt to make the death appear to be suicide.“During interrogation, Kailash confessed to killing his daughter. We arrested and remanded him on Thursday,” the SP said.
Article Summary: 18-year-old A Kalyani was reportedly killed by her father in Adilabad for refusing an arranged marriage. Her father allegedly smothered her to death while she slept, hanged her body from a roof beam to pass it off as suicide.

Ireland are set to make history in January 2027 when their men's side tours Pakistan for the first time, with a six-match 50-over series scheduled in Lahore as part of their preparations for the ICC World Cup Qualifier.Cricket Ireland on Thursday confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9 for a series running from January 13 to 24, with all six matches to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore.The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The matches will be played on January 13, 15 and 17 against the Shaheens, before the two teams meet in the ODIs on January 20, 22 and 24. Match timings are yet to be confirmed.While this will be the first visit to Pakistan by the Ireland men's side, it will not be the first tour by an Irish cricket team. The Ireland women's side visited the country in 2022 and famously won the T20I series.The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February 2027, which will be held in South Africa and Namibia.Graeme West, Cricket Ireland's Director of High Performance, underlined the importance of the tour in providing the one-day squad with valuable match practice ahead of the qualification campaign.“This is an extremely important tour for our One-Day squad as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifiers in February. Following the nine games played in the second half of 2026, a further six 50-over matches against quality opponents will support the players readiness for the qualifier taking place in South Africa and Namibia.“While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027.“Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope.”The Pakistan Cricket Board had initially planned a triangular series involving Ireland, Pakistan and Zimbabwe. However, Zimbabwe subsequently withdrew, citing its inability to travel to Pakistan. The revised arrangement will see Ireland play two separate three-match assignments instead.Ireland and Pakistan have faced each other seven times in men's ODIs, with Pakistan winning five matches, Ireland claiming one victory and one encounter ending in a tie.Ireland's only win remains one of the most memorable results in its cricketing history. It came during the 2007 World Cup in the Caribbean, when Ireland stunned Pakistan to knock the former champions out of the tournament.Pakistan, meanwhile, will enter the series after winning the ODI tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi and Lahore last month, under the captaincy of Shaheen Shah Afridi The six-match series will also offer Pakistan valuable preparation ahead of its international assignments in 2027, including the ODI World Cup later in the year.
Article Summary: Cricket Ireland confirmed that the team will arrive in Pakistan on January 9. The tour will comprise three 50-over matches against Pakistan A, known as the Shaheens, followed by a three-match ODI series against the senior Pakistan side. The six-match assignment assumes particular significance for Ireland as they prepare for the ICC World Cup Qualifier in February.

Article Title: A life in music, movement and memory
Article Text:
A still from the play

- Anvita Singh

Want us to review your play? Mail us at tims.delhitimes@timesofindia.com





How does an actor transform into a celebrated artiste on stage while depicting different stages of his life, and still make it convincing, all within 90 minutes? This was the question that lead actor Yohan Chacko had at the beginning of the play Enchantment: A Journey with Pandit Ravi Shankar as he interacted with playwright and director Gowri Ramnarayan, which cleverly served as a meta kind of opening to the play.However, Chacko ended up doing exactly that, making us forget for some time that this was not the sitar maestro himself. This willing suspension of disbelief was made possible by Ramnarayan, who took the audience on an inner journey into Ravi Shankar 's mind, while also not whitewashing his weaknesses and womanising ways.The rest of the play is as unconventional as the opening, punctuated and complemented by the lovely dance sequences performed by Sayani Chakraborty and Meera Sreeraj. The narrative mostly unfolds through the conversations between Yohan and Gowri, who had interviewed Ravi Shankar. Gowri is portrayed with both vivacity and emotional intelligence by actor Aarabi Veeraraghavan.The musical drama traces Shankar's birth, his subsequent affairs with both the sitar and the many women in his life. However, some of these episodes invite laughter from the audience in a way that feels uncomfortable, particularly when his philandering is treated as comic relief.His regrets about not giving his son the necessary care and attention, and his bond with his guru Allauddin Khan are also highlighted. The audiences follow Ravi Shankar and his multilayered story from Benares to Paris to US and back to India.While the production is woven around his biographical story, it is the dances that bring novelty to the storytelling. The sequences depicting the musician's first love and his solo act in front of a Parisian crowd, in which he plays Chitrasena, the Gandharva in Indra's court are precise and powerful, making the latter one of the standout segments of the drama.Predictably, there are references to his collaboration with The Beatles, his performance at the 1969 Woodstock festival and his much talked about rivalry with Ustad Vilayat Khan.The eventual interview between Shankar and Gowri Ramnarayan also brings the framing device full circle, offering glimpses of his thoughts on the musicians and collaborators who shaped his international journey.
Article Summary: Enchantment: A Journey with Pandit Ravi Shankar is directed by Gowri Ramnarayan. The musical drama traces Shankar's birth, his affairs with both the sitar and the many women in his life. While the production is woven around his biographical story, it is the dances that bring novelty to the storytelling.

Article Title: In 2017, a child who had no neurological complications at birth was left 100% disabled, bedridden after treatment at Delhi's Fortis Hospital, parents alleged; years later, an NMC-DGHS inquiry found 2
Article Text:
A joint inquiry by the National Medical Commission and Delhi government's health services found two doctors at Fortis Hospital unqualified.





NEW DELHI: A joint inquiry by National Medical Commission (NMC) and Delhi govt's directorate general of health services (DGHS) has found that two doctors at Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, do not meet the requirements to perform specialist duties in India. The committee has recommended that Delhi Medical Council (DMC) remove one doctor's additional qualification from its register.The inquiry followed a complaint by the parents of a child who developed cerebral palsy, epilepsy and West syndrome after being treated at the hospital in 2017. His mother had alleged medical negligence. However, DMC's disciplinary committee found no negligence attributable to the doctors in 2019. The subsequent proceedings, however, raised questions about their professional qualifications.In its report dated Nov 13, submitted to Delhi High Court along with NMC's affidavit on Nov 18, the committee said Dr Vivek Jain's MRCPCH qualification from UK did not make him eligible for specialist registration in India. It noted he did not hold a certificate of completion of training and was not on UK's specialist register.It recommended DMC deregister the MRCPCH qualification, which had been recorded as an additional qualification in 2016.The committee found Dr Akhilesh Singh's claimed Diploma in Child Health, obtained from Indian College of Maternal and Child Health, Calcutta, wasn't recognised by MCI/NMC and couldn't be registered as an additional qualification. It concluded he couldn't perform specialist duties in India.Fortis, in its response to NMC, said Dr Singh assisted the paediatrics team under the supervision of qualified consultants and didn't independently practice as a specialist. It said Dr Jain's designation as senior director and unit head was an internal administrative position and didn't imply recognition of any additional qualification.Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, declined to comment, saying the matter was sub judice.The inquiry was conducted following the directions of HC, which had sought scrutiny of the doctors' qualifications. In its affidavit, NMC informed HC that the joint probe had been completed and sought disposal of the contempt proceedings.The parents of the child alleged their son, Devarsh Jain, had no neurological complications at birth but suffered severe brain damage under the care of the two doctors at Fortis. They claimed Dr Jain was presented to them as a neonatologist and Dr Singh as a paediatrician, despite neither having the requisite specialist qualifications. They said the alleged misrepresentation and treatment left their son 100% disabled, bedridden and in a vegetative state.
Article Summary: A joint inquiry by the National Medical Commission and Delhi govt's health services found two doctors at Fortis Hospital unqualified.
